Let
\[
u=x-y^2.
\]
Then
\[
u'=\dot x-2y\dot y.
\]
A direct simplification gives the decoupled system
\[
\dot y=-y\bigl((y-2)^2+2a-b\bigr),
\]
\[
\dot u=-u\bigl((u-1)^2+5-a-2b\bigr).
\]
The change of variables \((x,y)\mapsto(u,y)=(x-y^2,y)\) is a global homeomorphism, so \((x,y)\to(0,0)\) iff \((u,y)\to(0,0)\).

For a scalar equation
\[
\dot z=-z\bigl((z-r)^2+s\bigr),
\]
the origin is globally asymptotically stable on \(\mathbb R\) exactly when \(s>0\). Indeed, if \(s>0\), then the bracket is always positive, so \(z(t)\) always moves monotonically toward \(0\), remains bounded, exists for all \(t\ge 0\), and satisfies
\[
|z(t)|\le |z(0)|e^{-st}.
\]
If \(s\le 0\), the bracket has a real zero, giving a nonzero equilibrium, so global convergence to \(0\) is impossible.

Applying this to the two scalar equations requires
\[
2a-b>0
\]
and
\[
5-a-2b>0.
\]

Therefore the equilibrium \((0,0)\) is globally asymptotically stable exactly for
\[
\boxed{\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:\ b<2a\ \text{and}\ a+2b<5\}.}
\]
